final_steps: 1.1 Put $t_n := b - (b-a)/(n+2)$. Then $a < t_n < b$ for every $n$ and $t_n \uparrow b$. Because $(a,b) = \bigcup_n (a,t_n]$, continuity from below and give $$\mu_F((a,b)) = \lim_n \mu_F((a,t_n]) = \lim_n \big(F(t_n) - F(a)\big) = F(b^-) - F(a).$$ Here $F|_{[a,b]}$ has bounded variation because it is nondecreasing, so ensures that the displayed left limit exists. [L1, L2, L3, algebra]

2.1 Put $s_n := a - 1/(n+1)$. Then $s_n < a$ and $s_n \uparrow a$, while the intervals $(s_n,b]$ decrease to $[a,b]$. The first interval has finite measure because $F$ is real-valued, so continuity from above and give $$\mu_F([a,b]) = \lim_n \mu_F((s_n,b]) = \lim_n \big(F(b) - F(s_n)\big) = F(b) - F(a^-).$$ The restriction $F|_{[a-1,a]}$ has bounded variation because it is nondecreasing, so ensures that the displayed left limit exists. [step 1.1, L1, L2, L3, algebra]

3.1 The intervals $(s_n,a]$ decrease to $\{a\}$, and continuity from above gives $\mu_F(\{a\})=F(a)-F(a^-)$. Indeed, $(s_0,a]$ has finite measure and $$\mu_F(\{a\})=\lim_n\mu_F((s_n,a])=\lim_n\big(F(a)-F(s_n)\big)=F(a)-F(a^-).$$ The same argument gives $\mu_F(\{b\})=F(b)-F(b^-)$. Therefore $$\mu_F([a,b)) = \mu_F([a,b]) - \mu_F(\{b\}) = F(b^-) - F(a^-).$$ Together with step 1.1, this proves all four interval formulas. [step 2.1, L1, L2, L3, step 1.1, L6, algebra]
4.1 By step 3.1 and , the point $a$ is an atom of $\mu_F$ exactly when $\mu_F(\{a\}) = F(a) - F(a^-) > 0$, which is exactly the jump condition $F(a) > F(a^-)$. [L5, step 3.1]

5.1 Fix $m \ge 1$. The restriction $F|_{[-m,m]}$ is nondecreasing, hence of bounded variation on $[-m,m]$. So makes its discontinuity set at most countable. Every atom of $\mu_F$ in $(-m,m)$ is an interior jump point by step 4.1, hence lies in that countable discontinuity set. Therefore the atoms in $(-m,m)$ are at most countable. By , their union over $m\ge1$ is at most countable, and this union contains every atom of $\mu_F$. [step 4.1, L3, L4, given]
6.1 Steps 1.1 through 5.1 prove the claimed interval formulas, the atom criterion, and the countability of the atom set. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎
